Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants should note that the Q&A session will be conducted via the telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables Inc.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Development Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Solara Renewables Inc. had a strong third quarter, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements. First, favorable PPA pricing trends and proactive contract extensions that solidify our revenue stability. Second, prudent management of debt levels and financing costs to support our expansion. Third, the meaningful impact of government incentives and subsidies accelerating our project economics. Fourth, robust revenue and earnings growth driven by execution across our core segments. And fifth, exciting development pipeline additions and project milestones that expand our future capacity.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased with our financial results for the third quarter. Revenue reached $1.75 billion, representing a 45% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 29.4%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $350 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $180 million, or $0.95 per diluted share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Let me dive deeper into some of those key aspects Jordan mentioned, starting with PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, which remain the bedrock of our revenue stability. Power Purchase Agreements represent about 85% of our contracted backlog here at Solara Renewables, with our portfolio spanning 12 GW of operating solar, wind, and hybrid assets across North America, Europe, and emerging APAC markets. These trends directly underpin our full-year 2024 guidance of $2.8 to $3.0 billion in adjusted EBITDA.

On PPA pricing trends, we've observed continued softening in headline prices over the past 12 months, driven by deflation in hardware costs and technological efficiencies, though stabilization is emerging in key regions due to inflationary pressures on operations and maintenance, supply chain resilience efforts, and surging corporate demand for decarbonization. Globally, the average contracted PPA price for new utility-scale solar projects was $26 per MWh in Q3—a 12% year-over-year decline from $29.50 per MWh, aligning with NREL's latest benchmarks. For wind, prices held at $32 per MWh, down 8% year-over-year, as turbine cost reductions slowed following 2023 supply chain bottlenecks.

Regionally, dynamics vary. In the US, ERCOT leads with solar PPAs averaging $22 per MWh for recent bids—sub-$20 per MWh in Texas for high-irradiance sites achieving 28% plus capacity factors using our TOPCon bifacial modules. We've secured 450 MW of new PPAs there at a $23 per MWh blended rate, beating levelized cost of energy estimates by 15%. In contrast, PJM and MISO see prices at $28 to $30 per MWh, up 5% quarter-over-quarter, as buyers like Google and Amazon incorporate PTC inflation adjustments under IRA guidance. Our hedge ratio for US assets is 92%, minimizing merchant exposure amid volatile hub prices.

In Europe, the post-Ukraine energy crisis has driven premiums, with German and Spanish PPAs at $45 to $55 per MWh, up 18% year-over-year, fueled by transmission system operator curtailment risks and EU REPowerEU mandates. We've locked in 300 MW of hybrid solar-plus-storage PPAs in Iberia at €48 per MWh—or about $52 per MWh equivalent—incorporating four-hour battery energy storage system dispatch to capture peak pricing under Spain's RD 413 framework. UK auctions via CfD round six averaged £47 per MWh—or $60 per MWh—where our 200 MW portfolio extension benefited from unsubsidized bids.

In APAC, India's SECI auctions reached record lows at ₹2.50 per kWh—or $30 per MWh—down 15% year-over-year, thanks to 600W-plus monoperc panels and 25% domestic content rules. We've added 600 MW to our Rajasthan pipeline at this level, achieving internal rates of return north of 12% post-FIT escalation clauses.

Turning to contract extensions, we're capturing upside and de-risking our 20-plus GW development pipeline. In Q3, we executed extensions on 1.2 GW of legacy assets, or 15% of our operating fleet—securing five- to ten-year tails at an average eight- to 12% premium to original terms. For example, our 400 MW California solar farm, originally at $45 per MWh in 2015, was extended with PG&E at $52 per MWh, including CPI escalators and a 200 MWh four-hour Fluence battery for resource adequacy capacity payments under CAISO. This lifts unlevered IRR by 200 basis points to 9.5%.

In the Nordics, we extended 350 MW of onshore wind with Vattenfall at SEK 450 per MWh—or $42 per MWh—a 10% uplift, leveraging 45% capacity factors from V136-4.2 MW Vestas turbines upgraded with vortex generators. Our total extension backlog now stands at $1.5 billion in net present value terms, with 70% fixed-price and the balance indexed to Euribor or SOFR plus a two- to three-percent collar.

Technical initiatives include shifting to n-type TOPCon and HJT modules, cutting balance-of-system costs by 20% and enabling 30% plus DC:AC ratios without clipping losses. Hybridization is central—60% of new PPAs include storage, qualifying for ITC bonuses up to 50% under IRA domestic content adders. We're piloting AI-driven O&M through our SolaraOS platform, targeting two- to three-percent yield uplifts to support extension premiums.

This positions us for asymmetric upside, with PPA prices bottoming—a global floor at $24 per MWh for solar by 2025 per BloombergNEF—while extensions lock in inflation hedges and preserve 20-30% merchant tail exposure for high-margin opportunities in ERCOT and NEM Australia. Risks like interconnection queues and Chinese module tariffs are mitigated by our 95% US-sourced supply chain. Overall, this supports our 15- to 18-percent ROIC target and $0.45 to $0.50 per share dividend growth.

Next, on debt levels and financing costs, which anchor our capital structure in this capital-intensive sector. As leaders in utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind, and BESS, our financing fuels our 15 GW pipeline while optimizing costs amid volatile rates and policy tailwinds.

As of September 30th, gross corporate and project-level debt was $5.2 billion, up eight% year-over-year from $4.8 billion, mainly from $1.1 billion in construction financing for 2.5 GW of new solar-plus-storage projects in the US Southwest and Texas ERCOT. After $450 million in cash equivalents—bolstered by PPA monetizations—net debt is $4.75 billion. Some 65% of debt ties to operational assets with predictable cash flows from 18-year average remaining PPAs.

Leverage improved with net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA at 3.4x, from 4.1x last year and 3.7x in Q2, ahead of our 3.5x target. This stems from 22% year-to-date EBITDA growth to $1.4 billion, supported by 95% plus wind capacity factors and IRA tax credit realizations—more conservative than peers like Orsted at 4.2x or Vestas at 3.8x.

Financing costs saw our weighted average interest rate dip to 4.15% from 4.85% last year—a 70 basis point gain—yielding $215 million annualized interest expense, or 18% of adjusted EBITDA. Fixed-rate debt is 82%, with a 3.9% average coupon and 7.2-year blended maturity, shielding from Fed hikes. Floating exposure—SOFR plus 175 bps on $900 million construction draws—is fully hedged via swaps to 2027.

In Q2, we issued a $1 billion green bond—the largest by a pure-play US solar developer—at 3.75% yield, 25 bps inside prior curves, driven by ESG demand from BlackRock and CalPERS. This extends average maturity to 5.8 years, with no major corporate maturities until $450 million in 2026, pre-refinanced via forward-start swaps. Project financing is non-recourse: our latest 800 MW Texas BESS closed at SOFR plus 140 bps, backed by merchant stacks including ERCOT capacity payments and our AI battery optimization boosting efficiency to 92%.

In the US—75% of assets—40% of debt is sustainability-linked loans tied to KPIs like 25% Scope 1/2 emissions cuts, averaging L plus 160 bps versus 200 bps pre-IRA. Europe—15% of debt—saw €500 million EIB-backed wind repower at EURIBOR plus 110 bps. APAC JVs in India leverage IFC guarantees at INR SOFR plus 200 bps.

We're tapping the $1.2 trillion global clean tech debt market, with a $2 billion ATM for sub-4% green notes and algorithmic hedging at 3.5% on 60% of 2025-2027 floating. Liquidity is $1.8 billion, including $1.2 billion undrawn revolvers, for 24 months runway. We expect net debt-to-EBITDA at 3.0x by year-end 2025 as 4 GW CODs ramp, costs at 4.0% with Fed cuts—this supports 20% IRR on builds and derisks against polysilicon inflation or permitting delays.

Shifting to the impact of government incentives and subsidies, these are foundational, contributing over 25% to our adjusted EBITDA in Q3, up from 18% last year—unlocking $147 million in Q3 tax credits and subsidies, or 28% of segment EBITDA, from a 42% year-over-year PTC/ITC increase on 1.2 GW new assets. Cumulative US claims hit $420 million past 12 months, with $1.2 billion pipeline ahead.

The IRA's PTC/ITC extensions to 2032 supercharge us: wind PTC at $27.50 per MWh in 2024 jumps to $41.25 with adders—10% domestic content (100% US steel, 85% modules), 10% energy communities, yielding $38 per MWh blended on our 450 MW Brazos Wind expansion, LCOE at $22 per MWh, 35% below unsubsidized. Solar ITC: 30% base on four-hour BESS yielded $92 million for 800 MWh, monetized 95% via tax equity with Clearway, cutting CapEx 22%. Standalone storage at 30-50% ITC for 1.4 GWh pipeline.

State boosts: Texas CREZ and $5 billion RECs added $18 million; California SGIP up to $1,000/kWh; New York NY-Sun 15% module reductions. US is 82% of benefits. Europe REPowerEU €300 billion unlocked €55 per MWh CfDs for Baltic offshore, €22 million EEG in Q2. CBAM from 2026 favors our 55% capacity factor turbines. APAC: China subsidies cut modules 40% to $0.22/W; India PLI for Gujarat hybrids at $18/MWh LCOE.

Clean hydrogen: IRA 45V PTC $3/kg for our 100 MW New Mexico pilot, pre-sold 50,000 tons, DOE MACH2 $50 million adds $200 million grants. Global subsidies $1.3 trillion in 2023 fueled 510 GW adds. Risks like elections mitigated by 11% IRR at 50% haircut, via 70% fixed PPAs.

We're diversifying to 45% storage-hybrids, $800 million US factories for adders, $2.5 billion tax equity. Incentives drive $600-700 million 2024 benefits, lifting EBITDA to $2.1-2.3 billion.

Finally, on revenue and earnings growth: Q3 revenue $1.75 billion, up 45% YoY and 20% QoQ; adjusted EBITDA $420 million, 40% YoY, margins 24%; net income $180 million, $0.95/share, 55% growth. EPC/development 55% at $960 million, up 60%—2.3 GW solar like 850 MW Desert Bloom with IRA 45X/PTC, CAPEX $0.82/W; wind $400 million, 1.1 GW GE 6.X at 15% capacity factors.

Storage 20% $350 million, 110% YoY on 1.8 GWh like 500 MWh Ironwood LFP/vanadium; margins 32% on $85/kWh cells. Services/O&M $160 million, 28% up, 95% availability via NexOS.

North America 62% $1.1 billion +55%; Europe 22% +38%; APAC 12% +25%; LATAM 4%. Gross margins 29.4% +320 bps on scale, TOPCon BOS cuts; SG&A 7.2%. ROIC 11.2%. Hybrids 40% pipe, R&D $150 million on H2/perovskite. Guide Q4 $1.9-2.0 billion, FY $7.2-7.5 billion.

Now, I'll pass the call to Mike Thornton to discuss our project development pipeline.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 18.4 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

In Q3, we advanced 3.2 GWdc into late-stage, a 28% quarter-over-quarter increase to total 18.4 GWdc in solar, wind, BESS, and green hydrogen—ahead of 10-12 GW annual adds, driven by hyperscalers at 35% of offtake talks.

Solar led with 2.1 GWdc, including 1.2 GWdc Desert Bloom Southwest TOPCon at sub-$25/MWh LCOE with IRA ITC. BESS +800 MW/3.2 GWh four-hour LFP, like 400 MW/1.6 GWh Ironwood Texas stacking ERCOT revenues. Wind 200 MW GE 6.X; H2 100 MW Plug Power.

US 65% (2.1 GW), PJM/MISO de-risked 1.5 GW; Europe 20% (640 MW) Borken 300 MW approved; international 15% (480 MW) India/Australia hybrids.

Milestones: 12 inflection points de-risking 4 GW. FID/NTP 1.1 GW like 750 MWdc Sagebrush +300 MW/1.2 GWh Nevada PPA $22/MWh COD Q4 2025. 85% US approvals; energized 450 MW PJM BESS $150/kW capacity. 2.3 GW PPAs including 500 MW hyperscaler; Dutch 200 MW offshore TSO. First 100 MW HJT 23.5% eff; H2 60 MW testing $1.50/kg.

Hub-and-spoke in REZs cuts delays 40%; 45% domestic content; 3-4 GW H2 adds, 2 GW NTP year-end, 15-18% IRR for 4-5 GW annual starts.

Next, Elena Vasquez will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions by 25% year-over-year through advanced turbine upgrades and solar tracking optimizations, improving our energy efficiency with AI-driven predictive maintenance achieving 98% uptime across our fleet, and promoting responsible resource management via water recycling in BESS cooling systems that cut usage 40%. We are also actively involved in community engagement, supporting local workforce training in renewable hubs and funding biodiversity offsets near project sites. We believe that our sustainability efforts not only benefit the environment but also create long-term value for our stakeholders.

I'll now turn the call back to Jordan for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Elena. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Instructions for the Q&A session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Green Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Mike Thornton:
Thanks for the question, John. Supply chain constraints remain a headwind, particularly around polysilicon and turbine components amid Red Sea disruptions and Chinese export controls. However, we've mitigated this through our 95% US-sourced strategy, locking in 80% of 2025 steel via forwards and qualifying for full IRA domestic content bonuses. This has kept our interconnection delays under 12 months versus industry 36-plus, as seen in our recent NTPs for Sagebrush and Ironwood. We're also diversifying with JVs in India for modules and maintaining 24-month inventory buffers, so Q4 CODs remain on track with no material slippage expected.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with EcoInvest. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Jordan Hale:
Great question, Lisa. Emerging markets like India, Australia, and LATAM represent 15-20% of our pipeline growth, targeting 25% CAGR through 2027. In India, we're leveraging SECI lows and PLI for 600 MW Rajasthan at 12% plus IRRs; Australia NEM for 250 MW NSW hybrids with REZ subsidies; Brazil floating solar pilots. Strategy emphasizes JVs for local content—IFC guarantees keep financing at SOFR plus 200 bps—and stacking incentives like India's 20% production-linked. We de-risk via 70% PPA pre-sales to corporates, hedging currency with collars, positioning for $18/MWh LCOEs while navigating policy flux.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with RenewBank. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Jordan Hale:
David, competition is intensifying, but our edge lies in hybrids and tech differentiation—40% of pipe is solar-storage-wind, slashing queues and qualifying for stacked ITC/PTC. We've outpaced peers with 18.4 GW pipeline via hub-and-spoke in REZs, proprietary SolaraOS for 2-3% yield uplifts, and fortress balance sheet at 3.4x leverage. Vertical integration in O&M and domestic supply cuts costs 20%, while 92% hedge ratio shields revenues. M&A/partnerships like our hyperscaler PPAs add asymmetric scale, targeting 15-18% ROIC above industry averages.

Operator:
Instructions for the Q&A session. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for any closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Solara Renewables Inc. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
